PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.1,44,303/- awarded by the Tribunal,
is in appeal.
2. The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.
3. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has sustained fracture of left tibia and cut injuries to her forehead and other injuries all over the body.

4. The Tribunal has thereafter awarded the following sums as compensation :
 Sl.

Particulars Amount  No.
 In (Rs.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 40,000/-
 2. Actual Medical expenses 13,823/-
 3. Future Medical expenses 20,000/-
 4. Special diet and conveyance 10,000/-
 5. Permanent disability 60,480/-
 Total 1,44,303/-

5. The Tribunal, on an analysis of the medical evidence, has concluded that the claimant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 9% to the whole body.
The Tribunal has assessed the disability at 9%.
In my view, having regard to the evidence of the Doctor, it would be appropriate to assess the whole body disability at 12%.
6. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.8,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which for the accident of the year 2017, would be Rs.11,000/-.
7. As the claimant was aged 61 years, a multiplier of '7' would have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,10,880/- (Rs.11,000/- x 12 x '7' x 12%) towards 'loss of future income'.
8. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.40,000/- towards 'pain and suffering and Rs.13,823/- towards 'medical expenses' and Rs.20,000/- towards 'future medical expenses'.
These sums are just and proper and therefore, affirmed.
9. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- towards 'special diet and conveyance, in my view, having regard to the length of hospitalization, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.20,000/-.
10. The Tribunal has not awarded any amount towards 'loss of income during laid-up period' and 'loss of amenities'.
In my view, it would be appropriate to treat laid-up period as three months and award Rs.33,000/- towards 'loss of income during laid-up period'.

Having regard to the fact of 12%
disability, it would be appropriate to award Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
11. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation :

Sl. Particulars Amount  No.
 In (Rs.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 40,000/-
 2. Medical expenses 13,823/-
 3. Future Medical expenses 20,000/-
 4. Special diet and conveyance 20,000/-

5 . Loss of income during laid-up 33,000/-
 period

6. Loss of amenities 40,000/-
 7. Loss of future income 1,10,880/-

14. On such deposit, the claimant is entitled to withdraw the same as per the terms of the award of the Tribunal.
15. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
